samples.summary: Frontend `seg()` invariant is advertised for "a document id, a folder id, a workspace id" but is only wired into documents.ts; every other frontend API module still interpolates ids raw
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:6 claims the rule covers folder and workspace ids, and docs/design/cli.md:1136-1140 states "The rule is not CLI-only … applied to the document routes". Unencoded interpolations remain at packages/frontend/src/api/folders.ts:10,24,42,64,82 (`/workspaces/${workspaceId}/folders`, `/folders/${id}`), workspaces.ts:48,75,88,102,143,212 (`${BASE}/${workspaceId}/api-keys/${keyId}`), share-links.ts:60,78,89, files.ts:22, analytics.ts:127, datasources.ts:45-104. The stated design rule (§10 of docs/design/cli.md) is therefore only partially satisfied on the frontend, and the module docstring overstates what ships.

samples.summary: `seg()` is implemented twice (CLI + frontend) although the repo already has a canonical shared URL primitive module, `@wafflebase/core/url`
samples.evidence: packages/core/src/url/index.ts is documented as the "Shared URL-safety primitive" hoisted precisely because per-package copies "had already begun to diverge", and docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:131 lists `./url` as a shipped subpath. The frontend already depends on `@wafflebase/core` (packages/frontend/package.json:57), so its copy of `seg()` (packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts) could have lived there; the CLI has no core dependency, which partly justifies its own copy, but the change leaves two copies of a rule the docs now describe as one shared invariant.

samples.summary: A frontend-side behavior change (new `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` + document routes) is documented only in the CLI design doc; docs/design/frontend.md is not updated
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1136-1140 documents the frontend id-encoding primitive inside the CLI doc's §10. The repo files design docs by subsystem (docs/design/README.md:152 lists frontend.md as the canonical frontend doc), so a reader of frontend.md will not find the invariant that now governs packages/frontend/src/api.

samples.summary: "Every command that talks to the backend routes its `!res.ok` branch through here" is not true: `login` still calls `fetch` directly and reports `HTTP <status>` in a plain message
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:56,75,92 call `fetch` directly and line 98 throws `Failed to fetch workspaces (HTTP ${wsRes.status})`, which surfaces as the generic `ERROR` code rather than the `HTTP_ERROR` classifier the doc/comment now promise (docs/design/cli.md error matrix). The invariant the change advertises has an unstated exception.

samples.summary: The new outbound-fetch guard is a hand-rolled private-address denylist, while the repo's existing precedent for fetching untrusted URLs is a host allowlist in the backend Miro importer
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/miro/miro.service.ts:27-35 documents the same threat (169.254.169.254, cluster-internal services) and solves it with EXACT/SUFFIXES host allowlisting. `isPrivateHost`/`unwrapIpv4Mapped` in packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts re-derive IP-range logic in a second, differently-shaped form; no shared module or design-doc reconciliation of the two approaches is offered.

samples.summary: The change entrenches a second URL builder rather than removing it: each command must remember to call `seg()` when assembling a dry-run path, with `assertNoDotSegments` as a backstop
samples.evidence: printDryRun now re-checks dot segments (dry-run.ts:44-51) because encoding is a per-call-site obligation spread over cells.ts, docs.ts, files.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts, tabs.ts and sheets-import.ts. Exposing the built URL from `HttpClient` (which already owns `base` and `seg()`) would make the preview structurally identical to the request instead of a parallel construction that can drift.

samples.summary: The diff bundles four independent concerns into one change (id segment encoding CLI+frontend, upstream error-envelope unification, image-fetch SSRF guard, download filename fallback)
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts (+196 lines of error classification), packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts (+100 lines of address guarding), packages/cli/src/files/download.ts (filename fallback change) and the two new `url.ts` modules share only a loose "untrusted input" theme. Absent an originating issue tying them together, each is separately reviewable and separately revertible; the combined diff also changes a documented public contract (exit code 2 → reserved, docs/design/cli.md:805-812) as a side effect.

finding.summary: Frontend `seg()` invariant is advertised for "a document id, a folder id, a workspace id" but is only wired into documents.ts; every other frontend API module still interpolates ids raw
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:6 claims the rule covers folder and workspace ids, and docs/design/cli.md:1136-1140 states "The rule is not CLI-only … applied to the document routes". Unencoded interpolations remain at packages/frontend/src/api/folders.ts:10,24,42,64,82 (`/workspaces/${workspaceId}/folders`, `/folders/${id}`), workspaces.ts:48,75,88,102,143,212 (`${BASE}/${workspaceId}/api-keys/${keyId}`), share-links.ts:60,78,89, files.ts:22, analytics.ts:127, datasources.ts:45-104. The stated design rule (§10 of docs/design/cli.md) is therefore only partially satisfied on the frontend, and the module docstring overstates what ships.

verdict.reason: The code facts are real (seg() is used only in documents.ts; folders.ts et al. interpolate ids raw), but the finding is not blocking under the design-fit/spec-conformance rubric. The canonical design doc explicitly bounds the frontend application of the rule: docs/design/cli.md:1137-1140 says the browser client "carries the same primitive (seg(), packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts), applied to the document routes" — the shipped scope matches the documented scope, so no stated rule is only "partially satisfied". The originating issue's acceptance criterion (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:70-73) scopes segment encoding to the CLI client ("No id the client interpolates into a request path — workspace, document, tab, cell ref"), and its Non-goals (:79-83) say nothing about frontend routes; frontend-wide encoding is not an acceptance criterion. No design doc is missing or parallel (cli.md §10 covers it), nothing duplicates an existing module, and no Non-Goal is exceeded — none of the rubric's `major` categories apply. What is left is (a) a module docstring whose illustrative phrasing ("a folder id, a workspace id") is broader than current call sites — a wording/taste issue, minor by kind and never blocking, and not "design-doc discipline" since it is not a docs/design/ file; and (b) unencoded ids in other API modules, which is security-lens hardening explicitly deferred by this lens.
